claims: C1: Models should honor user requests.
C2: This obligation is subject to an exception: a user request that conflicts with a developer-level instruction need not be honored.
C3: This obligation is subject to an exception: a user request that conflicts with a system-level instruction need not be honored.
C4: This obligation is subject to an exception: a user request that conflicts with a root-level instruction need not be honored.

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a request from an end user, carrying user-level instruction authority

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: L1 is a higher instruction authority level than L2, per the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer level of authority
concepts.inference: the clause names developer-level instructions as a conflict source, so a predicate for such instructions is needed

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the system level of authority
concepts.inference: the clause names system-level instructions as a conflict source, so a predicate for such instructions is needed

concepts.name: root_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the root level of authority
concepts.inference: the clause names root-level instructions as a conflict source, so a predicate for such instructions is needed

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R conflicts with instruction I, meaning honoring R would contradict what I directs
concepts.inference: the clause's exception turns on a conflict relation between a user request and a higher-level instruction

concepts.name: user_request
concepts.gloss: R is a request made by an end user

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause names developer-, system-, and root-level instructions, so each instruction must carry a level for the conflict comparison to range over

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the developer level of authority
I is an instruction at the system level of authority
I is an instruction at the root level of authority

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is not obliged because it conflicts with developer instruction %
honoring user request % is not obliged because it conflicts with system instruction %
honoring user request % is not obliged because it conflicts with root instruction %

closure.reason: the clause obliges honoring user requests generally and only excepts conflicts with higher-level instructions; silence about other cases leaves them permitted
the clause permits refusing a user request only when it conflicts with a higher-level instruction; it does not forbid refusal in other cases, so silence permits
